content: 1. Lopinavir levels or effects are reduced by rifampin due to its impact on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of loratadine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 3. Lorlatinib is contraindicated with rifampin as it significantly reduces its levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Discontinue strong CYP3A inducers for three plasma half-lives before initiating lorlatinib. 4. Rifampin reduces losartan levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Lovastatin levels or effects are decreased by rifampin through its action on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor effectiveness may be reduced when coadministered with rifampin due to decreased ivacaftor exposure (AUC reduced by 57%) via hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration. 7. Rifampin decreases lumateperone levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Lurasidone is contraindicated with rifampin as it reduces its levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. 9. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Maraviroc levels or effects are reduced by rifampin through its action on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Rifampin decreases marijuana levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Mavacamten is contraindicated with rifampin as it reduces its levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. 15. Rifampin reduces mavorixafor levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Medroxyprogesterone levels or effects are reduced by rifampin due to its impact on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely to prevent contraceptive failure. 17. Rifampin decreases mefloquine levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Melatonin levels or effects are reduced by rifampin through its action on hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Rifampin decreases meloxicam levels by increasing its metabolism via hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 20. Mestranol levels or effects are reduced by rifampin through its action on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug to prevent contraceptive failure. 21. Methadone levels or effects are reduced by rifampin due to its impact on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Rifampin decreases methylprednisolone levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Metoprolol levels are reduced by rifampin due to increased metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Rifampin decreases mexiletine levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Miconazole vaginal levels are reduced by rifampin through increased metabolism. This interaction applies only to the oral form of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 26. Rifampin reduces midazolam levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Midostaurin levels or effects are reduced by rifampin due to its action on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Rifampin decreases mifepristone levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Mipomersen and rifampin may increase each other’s toxicity due to their potential to elevate hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 30. Rifampin reduces mirtazapine levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Modafinil levels or effects are reduced by rifampin through its action on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 32. Rifampin decreases moexipril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 33. Momelotinib toxicity may be increased by rifampin due to its effect on OATP1B1/B3 transporters. Monitor closely for adverse reactions. 34. Montelukast levels or effects are reduced by rifampin through its action on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Morphine levels are reduced by rifampin due to increased metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 36. Nafcillin may antagonize the effects of rifampin against Staphylococcus aureus. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Rifampin reduces naldemedine levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Naloxegol is contraindicated with rifampin as it reduces its levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. 39. Rifampin decreases nefazodone levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Nelfinavir is contraindicated with rifampin as it reduces its levels or effects by increasing metabolism, potentially leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. 41. Rifampin reduces neomycin PO levels or effects by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Nifedipine levels or effects are reduced by rifampin through its action on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Rifampin decreases nilotinib levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 48. Nimodipine levels or effects are reduced by rifampin through its action on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Rifampin decreases nintedanib levels or effects by P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration, especially with P-gp inducers that are also CYP3A4 inducers. 50. Nirmatrelvir is contraindicated with rifampin as it reduces its levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to virologic failure.
